documents.title: INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: In FY 2025-26, Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported revenue from operations of Rs 78,610.66 crore and a profit after tax of Rs 3,061.85 crore. The company achieved a crude throughput of 11.71 MMT with a capacity utilization of 112% and a distillate yield of 79.1%. CPCL was elevated to Navratna status in June 2026 and launched its retail fuel operations with approval to set up 300 retail outlets. Furthermore, CPCL declared a dividend of Rs 62 per share while maintaining a debt-equity ratio of 0.18.

demand_outlook.claim: Rising urbanization, industrialization, and infrastructure growth in India are driving sustained demand for petroleum products.
demand_outlook.quote: India continues to be among the fastest-growing major economies in the world, with rising urbanization, industrialization and infrastructure development driving sustained growth in petroleum product demand.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL implemented 21 energy conservation schemes resulting in a 0.30% reduction in fuel and loss.
margins_costs.quote: 21 ENCON schemes 0.30% F&L reduction and 0.11MMT GHG reduction.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL recorded a crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and a distillate yield of 79.1% during FY 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: Despite undertaking planned maintenance activities in one of the crude refinery units, your Company achieved its highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and recorded a best-ever distillate yield of 79.1%.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a capacity utilization level of 112% during the financial year.

risks_headwinds.claim: The global energy sector experienced geopolitical uncertainties, changing market dynamics, and economic realignments.
risks_headwinds.quote: Against the backdrop of a transformative year for the global energy industry, marked by geopolitical uncertainties, evolving market dynamics, economic realignments and accelerating energy transition, your Company continued to demonstrate resilience, agility and operational excellence.

risks_headwinds.claim: A surge in crude oil and product prices towards the end of the year caused a temporary increase in working capital requirements.
risks_headwinds.quote: Mainly due to a surge in crude oil and petroleum product prices in international markets towards the year end, leading to higher working capital requirements, which is transient in nature.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
